cf.title: Crashes on a partition whose concurrent detach never finished
cf.authors: shveta malik (shvetam), Mihail Nikalayeu (mihailnikalayeu), Zsolt Parragi (zsolt.parragi)

input.subject: Crashes on a partition whose concurrent detach never finished

verdict_reasoning: The crash fixes are wanted bug fixes, and no objection at level 1a or 1b survived. The surviving objections (standards-compat-1, standards-compat-2, maintenance-fit-2) are all fixable and concern back-patching 0003 and 0004, which change replication output and locking in stable branches. Message #32 says the invalidation question needs more discussion, so the scope decision belongs to the committers engaged in the thread.

brief.title: Fix crashes and stale publication state for partitions pending concurrent detach
brief.problem: When the wait in DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY is interrupted, the partition keeps relispartition = true while get_partition_ancestors() returns nothing. Several callers assume a non-empty ancestor list and hit an assertion failure or NULL dereference. Users of logical replication and identity columns on partitioned tables are affected, and the walsender can enter a crash loop.
brief.proposed_design: Each caller checks the ancestor list instead of relispartition, and a partition pending detach is published as a standalone table, as after FINALIZE. getIdentitySequence() still climbs to the root, because the sequence belongs to it. The first detach transaction also invalidates the partition's relcache and its descendants', taking AccessShareLock on the descendants.
user_visible_surface: pg_publication_tables and pg_get_publication_tables() list a partition pending detach under publish_via_partition_root = true publications.
New DETAIL and HINT when a detach-pending partition is named in a publication EXCEPT clause (committed part).
Changes to a detach-pending partition are no longer replicated via the former root once its relcache is invalidated.
author_claims: A plain UPDATE on a detach-pending partition crashed the server in v19 without any publication; that fix is committed.
The pgoutput crash exists since v14, and fd366065e06a widened it to any FOR ALL TABLES publication, a v19 regression per Sawada.
Publishing via the former root would make publisher and subscriber data diverge, so standalone publishing is the chosen rule.
Without invalidation, whether a session sees old or new publication state depends on whether it touched the partition before the detach.
Each patch carries a test that reproduces the problem; the series is mostly AI-generated, per the author.
brief.thread_state: The v19 relcache crash fix (v1-0003) is committed; Zhijie Hou posted v3 of the pgoutput crash fix for PG15 through HEAD to close the open item, with Amit asking Sawada to confirm scope. The invalidation patch (0004) and the publication-list patch (0003) await more discussion, and CFbot reports a rebase is needed.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether 0004's extra invalidation and descendant locks have side effects beyond replication, which Shveta raised.
No one has settled whether 0003 and 0004 are back-patched or HEAD-only, despite Backpatch-through: 14 in their commit messages.
The proposal does not say whether a subscriber needs REFRESH PUBLICATION after upgrading to see detach-pending partitions.
The suggested HEAD-only change to get_partition_ancestors() taking a flag has no patch yet.
PG14 end of life on 2026-11-12 makes its back-patch target uncertain.

objections.title: Back-patching 0004 changes which rows replicate in a minor release
objections.failure_scenario: A publisher on PG15 has a FOR TABLE root publication with publish_via_partition_root = true, and one partition is stuck in detach pending. The subscriber receives that partition's changes through the root today. After a minor update with 0004, those changes stop arriving, and the subscriber finds out only when its rows no longer match the publisher's.
objections.argument: 0004 carries Backpatch-through: 14, but in message #32 Amit calls the invalidation question unrelated to PG-19 and in need of more discussion. In message #11 Shveta was unsure whether the extra invalidation has other effects. Moving from root-routed to standalone may be the right rule, as message #12 argues, but changing it in a stable branch alters replication output for users who did not ask for it. The thread has not agreed whether this is HEAD-only.
objections.author_must_show: Why is changing replication routing for detach-pending partitions acceptable in stable branches, instead of HEAD only with a release note?

critic.reasoning: The thread has not settled whether 0004 is back-patched; message #32 says it needs more discussion. The scenario's baseline holds only for sessions with a stale cache entry (message #11), but the routing change in a stable branch is still unanswered.

objections.title: 0003 changes pg_publication_tables output in stable branches without subscriber guidance
objections.failure_scenario: After a minor update, pg_publication_tables lists a detach-pending partition next to its root for publish_via_partition_root publications. A subscriber that has only the root table runs ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION. The refresh now needs a table the subscriber does not have, and the user finds out when the refresh fails or that partition's changes are skipped.
objections.argument: The 0003 commit message says it lets REFRESH PUBLICATION pick up the partition before FINALIZE, with Backpatch-through: 14. Today the documented outcome of publish_via_partition_root is that only the root is listed, and monitoring or schema-sync tools may rely on that. The proposal does not say what subscribers must do after the update, or whether a refresh is required. The brief lists both points as open.
objections.author_must_show: What must an existing subscriber do after the minor update, and how does the release note tell users that pg_publication_tables can now list a partition next to its root?

critic.reasoning: 0003 carries Backpatch-through: 14 and changes what pg_publication_tables lists. A refresh on a subscriber without the leaf table fails on the missing relation, and the proposal does not say what subscribers must do.

objections.title: Back-patching 0004 adds locking and invalidation to stable branches
objections.failure_scenario: After a minor upgrade, a user runs DETACH PARTITION ... CONCURRENTLY on a partitioned partition with thousands of leaves. The first transaction now takes AccessShareLock on every leaf. It can wait behind a leaf held in AccessExclusiveLock, or run out of shared lock table space, where it succeeded before the upgrade.
objections.argument: 0004 says Backpatch-through: 14, but Shveta in message #11 was not sure about side effects, and Amit in message #32 said the invalidation needs more discussion. The commit message explains the lock choice only against VACUUM. It does not cover lock count, wait behavior, or the cost of invalidation for large trees. A changed lock footprint in a minor release is a change that the project has to defend in every supported branch.
objections.author_must_show: What does the first DETACH CONCURRENTLY transaction now wait for or allocate on a partition tree with many leaves, and why is that acceptable in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Shveta's side-effect question from message #11 has no answer, and the first transaction gains a new wait on descendants. The lock-count part is weak, because the 0004 commit message notes that DetachPartitionFinalize() already takes AccessExclusiveLock on them.

refuted.title: Standalone publishing of a detach-pending partition can stop root-only subscribers
refuted.failure_scenario: A publisher with publish_via_partition_root = true serves a subscriber that has only the root t1. After an interrupted detach of t1_p2, 0001 and 0004 make pgoutput send t1_p2 changes under the name t1_p2. The apply worker likely finds no local t1_p2 and errors on every retry until someone runs FINALIZE or creates the table.
refuted.argument: The thread settled that publishing via the former root makes data diverge (message #12), and the proposal takes standalone publishing as the rule. It does not say what a subscriber that never had the leaf table gets in exchange. With 0004, this replaces stale but working routing with an apply error that starts as soon as the detach is interrupted. Before, the stale relcache kept routing those changes to the subscriber's root (message #11). A committer would likely ask whether that trade is right, especially in back branches.
refuted.author_must_show: What happens on a subscriber that has only the root table once a detach-pending partition is published under its own name, and is that acceptable in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: A root-only subscriber of a FOR ALL TABLES publication gets the same apply error after FINALIZE, or today after a walsender restart. Message #12 weighed root routing and rejected it for data divergence; the back-branch part is a duplicate of standards-compat-1.

refuted.title: Back-patched 0003 and 0004 change publication membership without subscriber guidance
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator applies a minor update to the publisher. pg_publication_tables now lists a detach-pending partition under a pubviaroot publication, and pgoutput stops routing its changes via the root. A subscriber that does not run REFRESH PUBLICATION drops those changes silently, and nobody notices until the data is compared.
refuted.argument: 0003 and 0004 carry Backpatch-through: 14, and both change which relations a publication covers and how their changes are named on the wire. Amit called the invalidation issue unrelated to v19 and said it needs more discussion (message #32). Nisha asked for a side-effect analysis (message #23). The 0003 commit message says that until REFRESH, the subscriber silently skips the partition's changes, but the proposal has no release-note or upgrade step that tells operators to refresh.
refuted.author_must_show: Should 0003 and 0004 go into HEAD only, and if they are back-patched, what must subscriber operators do after the minor update to avoid silently skipped changes?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for 0004 and of standards-compat-2 for 0003.

refuted.title: Per-caller checks leave the get_partition_ancestors() trap for future callers
refuted.failure_scenario: A future patch reads relispartition and takes llast_oid() of get_partition_ancestors(), as 509199587df7 and fd366065e06a each did. Regression tests rarely create a detach-pending partition, so the bug ships. A user with an interrupted DETACH CONCURRENTLY then hits an assertion failure or a NULL dereference.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows the same mistake in three independent places, and messages #6 and #22 found a fourth and a fifth. The series fixes each call site, but it leaves the API that invites the mistake. Alvaro in message #2 suggested a boolean argument so that each caller decides on purpose, and Amit in messages #7 and #8 deferred that to a HEAD-only patch. No patch for it exists yet, so HEAD keeps the trap for every new caller.
refuted.author_must_show: Will a HEAD-only change that makes callers handle the detach-pending state explicitly go in with this series, so the next new caller fails loudly instead of crashing?

critic.reasoning: Messages #2, #7 and #8 weighed the interface change and deferred it to a separate HEAD-only patch, because back branches cannot take a changed function signature. The missing follow-up is not a defect of these crash fixes.

refuted.title: 0003 changes publication membership in back branches without upgrade guidance
refuted.failure_scenario: A subscriber has only the root table, which is the usual setup with publish_via_partition_root = true. After a publisher minor upgrade, REFRESH PUBLICATION adds the detach-pending leaf. The subscriber has no such table, so the refresh or the apply worker errors until an operator creates it.
refuted.argument: The 0003 commit message frames the change as a fix because changes are skipped silently today. For a root-only subscriber, though, the patched behavior turns a silent skip into a hard error after a minor upgrade. Message #12 uses exactly this root-only topology as its example. The proposal does not say what such subscribers must do, or whether REFRESH is needed at all.
refuted.author_must_show: What happens on a subscriber that has only the root table when 0003 is applied to a stable branch, and is 0003 HEAD-only for that reason?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which has the same root-only subscriber and refresh scenario.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: pgoutput publishes a detach-pending partition as a standalone table, and 0004 changes when that takes effect.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: 0003 changes the rows that pg_publication_tables and pg_get_publication_tables() return; no catalog format changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: v2-0001 touches partition.c, and the suggested flag for get_partition_ancestors() would change a function that extensions can call.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0003 and 0004 carry Backpatch-through: 14 and change publication lists, replication routing and locking in stable branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each caller of get_partition_ancestors() must handle the detach-pending state itself; the HEAD-only interface change has no patch yet.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Are 0003 and 0004 meant for HEAD only, or for stable branches as their Backpatch-through: 14 lines say?
If 0004 is back-patched, why is it acceptable for a minor release to stop replicating a detach-pending partition's changes via the former root?
What must an existing subscriber do after the update when pg_publication_tables starts listing a detach-pending partition next to its root, and is REFRESH PUBLICATION required?
What does the first DETACH CONCURRENTLY transaction now wait for on a partitioned partition with many leaves, and does the extra invalidation affect anything beyond replication?
With PG14 at end of life on 2026-11-12, which branch is the oldest back-patch target for each patch?

committability.owner_note: Alvaro Herrera, who wrote concurrent detach, offered in message #2 to push the fixes; Amit Kapila reviews the logical replication parts.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed replication output and a new lock and invalidation step in DETACH CONCURRENTLY, in every supported branch if 0003 and 0004 are back-patched.
committability.author_follow_up: The authors posted v2 and v3 after review, and the v19 relcache fix is committed; this suggests they stay for fixes.

priority.reason: These are crash and correctness fixes for logical replication and identity columns on partitioned tables, with a walsender crash loop and a v19 open item. The patches are small, but 0003 and 0004 touch pgoutput, publication lookup and tablecmds.c, and their back-patch scope is not settled.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether 0004's AccessShareLock on descendants and the extra invalidation are safe against concurrent drops and large partition trees. Only 3 of 37 messages were visible, so later agreement on scope may exist.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: BUG #18741: Detaching a partition referencing a partitioned table fails with a trigger-related error
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alexander Lakhin reported that detaching a partition fails with an internal trigger error when the partition has a foreign key to a partitioned table and its new parent has no matching foreign key. Tender Wang and jian he discussed fixing this, mainly by rejecting such ATTACH PARTITION commands except where the partition references a non-partitioned table or its own parent's hierarchy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They contain the bug report and two design suggestions with no patch, review or decision, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.summary:

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 27162a64b386; this branch is in code freeze due to a
nearing release.  We can commit again after the release is out.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: propagating replica identity to partitions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make alter table ... replica identity on a partitioned table recurse to all partitions, and make new partitions take the parent's replica identity, mapping an index-based identity to the matching partition index. psql would also show the replica identity of partitioned tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it for lack of time, with work still left in the patch. pg_dump had to emit the replica identity only after the index exists in all partitions, and a bug reported by Dmitry Dolgov was still open. Reviewers agreed with the recursion; the author planned to resubmit for November.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I've not had time to work on this issue, and there are a few remaining problems in the patch; mostly that I will need to change the way pg_dump represents the replica identity so that it is only defined when the index is dumped in all partitions rather than immediately after creating the index.

precedents_retrieved.title: Verify true root on replicas with amcheck
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the regular bt_check_index() function in amcheck verify the true root of a B-Tree index, so the check also works on replicas. It does this by locking the metapage and the potential root page at the same time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Peter Geoghegan asked what true root corruption meant and what symptom it caused, and he did not want to commit a patch that holds multiple buffer locks without a strong justification. The patch also stopped applying, and David Steele returned it after no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Your patch looks like it gets it right (it won't deadlock with other
sessions that access the metapage), but I hesitate to commit it
without a strong justification.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent pg_basebackup running as root
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_basebackup refuse to run as root (except for --help/--version), matching the existing checks in initdb, pg_ctl and pg_upgrade, so it cannot create root-owned files in a data directory that the postmaster could not use. The change was not to be backpatched, as it alters behavior.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed by Michael Paquier and then reverted after a separate discussion that is linked but not included in the visible messages. The visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: use AV work items infrastructure for GIN pending list's cleanup
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves GIN pending list cleanup to an autovacuum work item, requested when the list reaches gin_pending_list_limit. Inserts and updates would then no longer pay for the cleanup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Masahiko Sawada pointed out that work items run only after an autovacuum run, so the pending list could grow far past gin_pending_list_limit while the same work item is registered again and again. He suggested a soft limit and a hard limit, removal of duplicate work items, and skipping the item if autovacuum already cleaned the index. The author had no time to finish a revised version, so he marked the entry "Returned with feedback" and planned to resubmit.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So if many insertions happen before executing the autovacuum
work item, we will end up greatly exceeding the threshold
(gin_pending_list_limit) and registering the same work item again and
again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Fix issues with Windows' stat() for files pending on deletion"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Fix issues with Windows' stat() for files pending on deletion"
Reverted commit(s): Fix issues with Windows' stat() for files pending on deletion
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 54fb8c7, as per the issues reported by fairywren
when it comes to MinGW because of the lack of microsoft_native_stat()
there.  Using just stat() for MSVC is not sufficient to take care of the
concurrency problems with files pending on deletion.  It may be possible
to paint some __MINGW64__ in the code to switch to a different
implementation of stat() in this build context, but I am not sure either
if relying on the implementation of stat() in MinGW to take care of the
problems we are trying to fix is enough or not.  So this needs more
study.

precedents_retrieved.title: Separate memory contexts for relcache and catcache
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves catcache and relcache entries out of CacheMemoryContext into their own child contexts, CatCacheMemoryContext and RelCacheMemoryContext, so that pg_backend_memory_contexts shows each cache's memory use. Later versions added more child contexts, such as PlanCacheContext, SPICacheContext and TypCacheContext, and a separate patch changed the initial context sizes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund's messages are not shown, but Jeff Davis reports Andres's concern that the extra contexts add memory fragmentation in each backend. Jeff saw rough consensus only for CatCacheContext and RelCacheContext, and the thread was still looking for ways to reduce the fragmentation. Rahila Syed and Ashutosh Bapat found little value in PlanCacheContext and SPICacheContext, which hold no allocations of their own. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback, citing the open feedback and concerns.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Andres's concern, IIUC, is that the additional memory contexts will cause additional fragmentation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Multi-column list partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds multi-column list partitioning, so that `partition by list (a, b)` takes partitions defined by value tuples such as `for values in (1, 2), (1, 5)`. It changes bound transformation, the bound data structures, tuple routing, partition pruning, NULL handling and, in a split second patch, partition-wise join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amul Sul questioned the pruning design. Range partitioning needs a prefix of the partition keys, but list partitions could also be pruned on later keys alone, and he judged the NULL handling in pruning to be wrong. Julien Rouhaud set the entry to Waiting on Author because of these concerns and a clang warning. The visible messages show no new patch or author reply before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I haven't studied the whole partition pruning code and don't know the complete code flow, but AFAICU, this is not the correct way to handle null value.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P2] was a revert for a release code freeze, which does not apply here, and [P3] routed inheritance children through a parent, which this proposal does not do; the thread rejects that routing in message #12. The earlier discussions the thread mentions (Nisha's report in message #4, the get_partition_root thread in message #5, Alvaro's API idea in message #2) are related open work, not rejections.
The crash fixes themselves raise no standards or compatibility concern. Both objections are about back-patching the behavior changes in 0003 and 0004.
No on-disk, WAL record or catalog format change is proposed. The v19 relcache fix and the pgoutput crash fix (v3-0001) look sound from this angle.

The series opens no new security exposure. It removes crashes that a table owner can trigger by cancelling a concurrent detach. The publication change follows the existing rule that a detached table in a FOR ALL TABLES publication is published on its own, and the extra AccessShareLock in 0004 is weaker than the lock FINALIZE already takes.
The crash fixes are wanted and engaged committers own them; objections cover the API trap and the stable-branch scope of 0003 and 0004.

The series fixes crashes and wrong publication state in core code paths (pgoutput, getIdentitySequence(), relcache, pg_publication), so no extension, hook or existing option can stand in for it. The only nearby workaround, DETACH PARTITION ... FINALIZE, ends the bad state but does not prevent the crashes, and walsender decodes already-written changes against historic catalogs.

Demand is not in doubt. These are crash and correctness fixes in shipped behavior: walsender crash loops and assertion failures. Several people hit them on their own: the author in stress testing, Nisha while testing another patch (message #4), Zsolt from an automated review (message #22), and Sawada in his own work (message #27). Committers treat the v19 part as an open item. The demand angle has no grounds to object; the open questions about 0004 side effects and back-patch scope belong to the design angle.
